annotations.title: Replace a document, keeping every link

description: Replaces the contents of a document already on HTMLRadar. Every existing link stays exactly as it is — same address, same settings, same reading history — and serves the new contents from the next time it is opened, so nobody is sent a second link. The new HTML is screened for phishing signals as every upload is, and the previous version stays listed in the document's version history on the website. Restoring an earlier version is not available, from Claude or on the website; to go back, replace the contents again with the earlier page. Recipients may already have read the old contents. Pass either the whole new page in `html`, or `edits`: pieces of text to find in the page get_document returned, each with its replacement and each appearing exactly once. Edits suit small changes to a large page, because only the changes travel. Images that need a login, expiring image addresses and local file paths do not load for readers of the link. Images embedded in the HTML as data URIs always do. On an update, get_document shows each embedded image as a short htmlradar-image reference; keep each one exactly as it is and HTMLRadar puts the image back, so only new images count towards the 5 MB limit.

announce.description: Tell readers what changed and alert subscribers. Omit to announce only when every live link is company-only; otherwise the replacement is quiet.

document_id.description: The document whose contents are being replaced. Every link to it keeps working.

edits.description: Changes to the page get_document returned, applied in order. Each `find` must appear exactly once in the page at that point. Between 1 and 200. Pass this or `html`.

find.description: Text in the page or passages get_document returned, copied exactly; it must appear exactly once in the whole page.

replace.description: The text that takes its place.

expected_version.description: The document's current version as you last saw it: get_document and list_documents show it, and each replace_document result gives the new one. When the document has been replaced since, nothing is replaced and the call says so, so newer work is never overwritten.

html.description: The new HTML markup, in full. It may keep the htmlradar-image references get_document returned. Pass this or `edits`, not both.

note.description: Optional note for an announced update, at most 140 characters.

request_id.description: Leave unset on a first attempt. When a previous call failed saying it may still have been applied, pass the request_id that error named: the retry then returns the first result instead of doing it twice.

name: replace_document
title: Replace a document, keeping every link
